items.title: Louis James Interview, 1959-05-25
items.q: I've never called myself a member of, uh, no band but Lewisty Man.

ctx.x: Well I've never called myself on the band as a member, you know, but I've played with him. I've never called myself a member of, uh, no band but Lewisty Man. Mm-hmm. See, I only, yeah, that's the only band that I consider myself playing in a band, you know?
But you probably have played with a lot of other bands.

items.title: Emile Barnes, George Guesnon, Little Brother Montgomery, Harold Dejan Interview, 1961-03-11
items.q: this is gonna be with one of the real old timers, way back from 1927 with the Louis Domains band, and this is Louis James.

ctx.x: Hello jazz lovers, this is Creole George Gaynor, veteran New Orleans Dixieland jazz band jurist and guitarist, saying hello. On this tape, which I call just reminiscing with friends, will be heard the actual voices of some of the greatest personalities in New Orleans jazz. Some singing, some playing, some just talking, but all for kicks and off the record. Such as little brother Montgomery, the great jazz piano man and composer of the great blues classic Vicksburg Blues, who also dropped in from Chicago just in…

Well, you know, Curly, what's happening, my friend, brother George Gano? Well, hello, little brother Montgomery, and how are you? Well, you know, Curly, what's happening, my friend, brother George Gano? There ain't nothing happening, you come all the way from Chicago to see me, that's right? Well, in a way I did, I came down to see you, George Lewis, and Harold Dijon, and among you boys around, and my son, mostly I came to see, out of the Air Force, Hamilton Air Base, little brother Montgomery, his name is here…
